A ring, yellow-toned, stamped '14K PLUMB' or '14KP'.
Plumb 14K — exactly 14K (58.3%), no legal tolerance below.
A large plate has 'CLARICE CLIFF' or Bizarre pattern signature. Why?

Clarice Cliff — English Art Deco potter (1899-1972). Bizarre range highly collectible. Extensive fakes.

Clarice Cliff's Bizarre range (1929+) is highly collectible Art Deco pottery. Extensively faked. Genuine pieces have specific hand-painted characteristics. Reference authentication essential.
A TV listing photo shows the screen with dark cloudy patches in the corners.
Backlight bleed or clouding. Usually cosmetic; visible in dark scenes. Not repairable. Discount accordingly.
What does "NVMe form factor" mean in this context?
M.2 2280 / M.2 2242 / U.2 physical
A large workshop tool is a '3D PRINTER' with FDM or SLA technology. Why?

3D printer. Various technologies: FDM (filament), SLA (resin), SLS (powder). Consumer to professional.

3D printers: FDM (filament, common consumer) $200-3000; SLA (resin) $200-2000; SLS/DMLS professional. Various brands and quality tiers. Verify all functions and consumables.
What does "core / staples / everyday" mean in this context?
the always-in-stock basics
A phone listing photo shows the front screen with a large starburst crack originating from one corner. Why?

Screen crack — replacement is standard. Cost varies: $200-400 for Apple, $100-200 for third-party.

Screen replacement is common. Third-party parts often work fine but iPhone shows 'unable to verify parts' warning on newer models. Verify parts warranty from the shop.
A large tile has 'HENRY MERCER' or 'MORAVIAN' pottery signature. Why?

Moravian Pottery and Tile Works — American, 1898+. Henry Mercer founded. Arts and Crafts tile tradition. Collector market.

Moravian Pottery and Tile Works (Doylestown, PA, 1898+) is a distinctive American Arts and Crafts tile-maker. Henry Mercer founded. Still operating. Historical and contemporary tiles both collected.
A necklace with square links, minimalist appearance. Why?

Box chain.

Box chain has square cross-section links, giving a clean modern appearance. Popular for men's pendants and minimal contemporary jewelry.
A dresser has a mirror attached to a decorative frame at the top.
Traditional dresser with mirror. Various styles from Victorian through mid-20th century.

What deep pattern is shared between this scenario and the previous one?

The customer is at the counter holding an enameled dutch oven.
He's holding it and looking at his phone. He's been looking at
his phone for four minutes. He hasn't set the dutch oven down
and hasn't paid.

'How's the reviews looking,' Diego says.

The customer laughs a little, embarrassed.

'They're — mostly good. There's a couple of one-stars where
people say the enamel chipped after six months.'

'Yeah, that happens with a lot of them. Usually if they got
banged around in a metal-utensil household or went in and out
of really high heat. What's yours going to be doing.'

'Mostly stews. Sometimes bread.'

'Then you're fine. Stew doesn't stress enamel. Bread's hot but
you're not banging metal on it.'

'The reviews are so mixed though. This other one — hold on —
this one has fewer reviews but they're all five stars.'

He shows Diego the phone. Diego looks.

'Yeah. That one is fine too. It's a slightly cheaper enamel.
Same country of origin. Same weight. If you're looking at
five-star average versus four-point-two average, five-star
average with twenty-two reviews is basically noise. The
four-point-two with two thousand reviews is a real signal
about a real product used a lot of ways.'

'So you're saying — get this one.'

'I'm not saying anything. I'm saying the review math cuts a
different way than it looks. If you compare on the stuff that
matters for how you'll use it — enamel quality, heat
distribution, weight — this one and that one are close. This
one is thirty bucks more because the brand has been around
longer.

The person in front of you is deferring to an absent crowd; honor the fact of the crowd, offer information that speaks to both the person and the crowd, and don't ask them to override the crowd alone.
A ring, white-metal, marked '14K,' brilliant bright white. Why?

White gold, likely freshly rhodium-plated. Could also be palladium white gold (naturally whiter, less need for rhodium).

Palladium white gold is a modern alternative to nickel white gold — brighter naturally, less rhodium dependence, hypoallergenic. Mark alone does not distinguish.
A phone listing photo shows the box's serial number matching the phone's IMEI but the phone's serial number in About is 'F2LX...' while the box shows a phone-serial starting with 'D7QW...'

Box-and-device don't match. Different phones. Either box swap (usually for value inflation) or seller error. Box and device serials must match. IMEI matches (from IMEI printed on both) but device serials differ = someone swapped devices between boxes. If seller can't explain, reject.
A phone listing photo shows 'This iPhone Has Been Refurbished' notice.

Officially Apple-refurbished device. Comes with 1-year Apple warranty. Higher value than generic refurb. Apple Certified Refurbished carries the Apple 1-year warranty and full support. Third-party refurb varies wildly. Apple refurb pricing is usually 10-15% below new.
A phone listing shows 'Face ID has been reset' in Settings.

Face ID data cleared. Previous face data removed. New user can enroll their face without conflict. Positive sign — seller prepared properly. Resetting Face ID data (Settings > Face ID > Reset Face ID) removes stored face data. Should be done before resale. Along with iCloud sign-out, iMessage deregistration, and factory erase — standard resale preparation.
A tea bowl has an intentional single unglazed spot on the interior.

Japanese tea-ceremony piece. Some traditions include specific unglazed spots for wear or tradition. Japanese tea ceremony pottery has specific traditions — some pieces have intentional unglazed spots, deliberate imperfections (wabi-sabi aesthetic), or specific glaze effects. Not defects; intentional.
what's rocker?
chair with curved rockers
A large workshop tool is a 'PLANER' or 'THICKNESSER' with 20-inch capacity.

Large-capacity thickness planer. Handles wide boards. Professional or serious hobbyist tool. Motor and cutter head are key. Thickness planers reduce lumber to uniform thickness. Consumer sizes 12-13-inch; larger 15-20+ inch professional. Cutter head (straight blades vs helical) affects finish and blade maintenance.
